propositions: push non-fast-forward recovery's _recover_dirty_merge encounters the same untracked-overwrite wedge as reconverge: merge aborts when a local untracked file collides with a file the merge wants to create, leaving the store unrecoverable
the merge abort parser and quarantine mover from sync.py are reused to detect named collision paths and move them into a shared quarantine directory before retrying the merge once
the stash commit object is restored exactly once on all exit paths (success, retry-failure, non-recoverable abort) with no lost tracked edits
genuine content conflicts and unnamed collision paths retain today's abort-and-warn behavior unchanged
the quarantine move occurs between the failed merge and stash restore, and is guarded by a git status --porcelain fence to prevent relocation of tracked data
